source.title: Rethink the Connections among Generalization, Memorization, and the Spectral Bias of DNNs
source.authors: Xiao Zhang; Haoyi Xiong; Dong-Rui Wu

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a different primary measurement—local Fourier spectra—but trains networks under a noisy-label, extended-epoch setup and reports test-error curves that bear on epoch-wise double descent.
record.gate_note: The paper reports epoch-wise test-error curves for six model-and-dataset settings. It does not test test error as a function of sample size, establish a model-size double-descent curve, or test a single effective-complexity account. The width experiment reports that spectrum and test-error peak positions move together, not the fall-rise-fall shape across sizes. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Sections 2.2 and Figure 2 reproduce the deep-double-descent recipe (partial label shuffling, Adam lr 1e-4, extended training) and report test error by epoch for ResNet and VGG on SVHN, CIFAR10 and CIFAR100. That is the original's method and measure for V2. The spectral analysis is the paper's own addition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors state that the monotonicity of spectral bias fails: in late training, high-frequency components diminish, driven by a flatter off-manifold prediction surface. They say this 'leads to' the second descent of test error, a causal reading. They also claim the training-set spectrum is consistent with the test-set spectrum and can indicate the second descent without a test set.
record.recipe_differences: The setup is described as analogous to deep double descent and uses shuffled-label training over extended epochs. The study focuses on local Fourier spectra and uses its stated image datasets, architectures, and training settings rather than reporting a direct replication of the original study.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports different spectral behavior for VGG and ResNet and varies dataset, label-noise level, and model width. Its reported test-error double-descent curves in Figure 2 use 10% label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: In the toy task, on-manifold accuracy dips slightly after the perturbed point is memorized, while off-manifold accuracy keeps rising.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The late-training generalization gain comes from flattening the off-manifold prediction surface, not from on-manifold fit.

fits_no_version.finding: The epoch of the spectrum peak computed on training data correlates with the epoch of the test-error peak (Pearson 0.88, fit y=0.95x−6.59).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A label-free training-set spectral measure tracks the timing of the epoch-wise test-error peak.

fits_no_version.finding: As ResNet18 width varies, the spectrum peak moves with the epoch-wise test-error peak.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The spectral peak tracks how the epoch-wise double-descent peak shifts with width.

record.peer_reviewed: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence, 2020
record.problems: The reported test-error curves are figures without extracted numerical values or stated uncertainty. The detailed test-error curves use 10% label noise; the width result is reported as peak-position tracking rather than a test-error-versus-size shape. The authors report five runs for the peak-correlation experiments but no error bars or confidence intervals for the claim-relevant curves.

untested.parts: There is no curve of test error against model size. Appendix C varies width (0.5–2x) only to track the epoch of the test-error peak.
Test-error curves are shown only at 10% label noise. There are no numeric values or error bars, and the 0% noise appendix shows spectra only, with no test error.
Only deep CNNs are used. Other model classes and the capacity-risk curve are not tested.
No effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location across axes. EMC is only cited.
Label noise is described as used to strengthen double descent, but test error is not compared across noise levels. Regularization is not varied.
There is no re-parameterization of complexity.

missing.what: Figure 10(a) gives a test-error heat map over epoch × width (ResNet18, CIFAR10, 20% noise, 200 epochs), with marked test-error peaks at each width. This is a second epoch-wise test-error setting at 20% noise, with peak position varying by width. The text does not say whether a second descent follows in every width within 200 epochs.

The 20% label-noise runs (five runs each, six model-dataset pairs) yield T_E,peak values. However, the peaks are found by a patience-30 search, so these values do not by themselves show a fall-rise-fall curve.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche is set to T1 rather than T2. For V2 the measure (test error vs epoch) and recipe (label noise, Adam 1e-4, long training, ResNet18 on CIFAR10) match Nakkiran et al. closely, although the paper's focus is spectral. The authors call the pre-peak rise 'a little increase of the test error', so the peak is modest, but they explicitly identify it as epoch-wise double descent. No numeric test-error values are given anywhere.

versions.untested_parts: The width experiment tracks peak positions as width varies but does not report whether test error falls, peaks, and falls again as model size grows.
The reported epoch-wise curves use the specified noisy-label settings; other architectures, datasets, and training conditions are not tested.
The study does not vary the number of training samples near an interpolation threshold.
The study does not test double descent across model classes or assess a general capacity-risk curve.
It studies spectrum as an indicator of epoch-wise test-error behavior, but does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
Although label-noise levels are mentioned in supplementary spectrum figures, the study does not test whether noise or regularization drives, splits, or removes the test-error peak.
The study does not re-express complexity in terms of an effective number of parameters or test whether that removes the second descent.
